title: Fractions: Halves and Quarters
seo_title: Grade 1 Halves and Quarters Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Use and name fractions in familiar contexts including halves and quarters; solve and explain solutions to practical problems that involve equal sharing leading to solutions that include unitary fractions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 1 maths worksheets: equal parts, halves and quarters of shapes and amounts. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
key_sub: A quarter is smaller than a half.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A half is 1 of 2 equal parts; a quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts.
  • The parts must be the same size.
  • Half of 10 is 5: share 10 into 2 equal groups.
  • A quarter is smaller than a half.

Examples

Example

Half of 8

share 8 into 2 groups

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Unequal partsHalves must be equal.
Bigger or smallerA quarter is smaller than a half.
Counting partsCount the items in one part.

sets.title: Half or quarter of an amount

items.q: Find half of 4 counters.
items.e: Share the 4 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 2. 2 + 2 = 4. So half of 4 is 2.

items.q: Find half of 6 sweets.
items.e: Share the 6 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 3. 3 + 3 = 6. So half of 6 is 3.

items.q: Find half of 8 counters.
items.e: Share the 8 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 4. 4 + 4 = 8. So half of 8 is 4.

items.q: Find half of 10 sweets.
items.e: Share the 10 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 5. 5 + 5 = 10. So half of 10 is 5.

items.q: Find a quarter of 4 sweets.
items.e: Share the 4 sweets into 4 equal groups. Each group has 1. 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4. So a quarter of 4 is 1.

items.q: Find a quarter of 8 counters.
items.e: Share the 8 counters into 4 equal groups. Each group has 2. 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. So a quarter of 8 is 2.

items.q: Find a quarter of 12 sweets.
items.e: Share the 12 sweets into 4 equal groups. Each group has 3. 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. So a quarter of 12 is 3.

items.q: Find a quarter of 16 sweets.
items.e: Share the 16 sweets into 4 equal groups. Each group has 4. 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16. So a quarter of 16 is 4.

items.q: Precious eats the green slice of pizza. How much of the pizza does she eat?
items.e: The pizza has 4 equal slices. Precious eats 1 of them. That is a quarter.

items.q: Ruan has the green part of the cake. How much does he have?
items.e: The cake has 2 equal parts. Ruan has 1 of them. That is a half.

items.q: Lungile breaks this chocolate bar in half. How many squares are in each half?
items.e: The bar has 8 squares. Half of 8 is 4, because 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Ofentse has half of a cake. Sibusiso has a quarter of the same cake. Who has more?
items.e: A half is 1 of 2 equal parts. A quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts. 4 parts are smaller. So Ofentse has more.

items.q: Which is bigger: half of an orange or a quarter of the same orange?
items.e: 4 is more than 2, but more parts means smaller parts. So a half is bigger.

items.q: Zinhle shares a pizza equally with 1 friend. How much does each one get?
items.e: Zinhle and 1 friend are 2 people. 2 equal parts are halves. Each one gets a half.

items.q: Kabelo shares a cake equally with 3 friends. How much does each one get?
items.e: Kabelo and 3 friends are 4 people. 4 equal parts are quarters. Do not forget to count Kabelo.

items.q: Thandi and Dumisani share 10 grapes equally. How many grapes does each one get?
items.e: Share 10 into 2 equal groups. 5 + 5 = 10. Each one gets 5.

items.q: What is half of 14?
items.e: 7 + 7 = 14, so half of 14 is 7.
